### Contributing guidelines

- [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- [x] I have updated 'mini.nvim' to latest version of the `main` branch

### Module(s)

mini.snippets

### Neovim version

0.11 (!at least latest Nightly build!)

### Description

TL;DR: It would be nice to force mini.snippets to use `filetype` instead of tree-sitter parser through buffer options.

Context:
I'm using [mfussenegger/nvim-ansible](github.com/mfussenegger/nvim-ansible) to detect ansible files. It set the filetype to `yaml.ansible` while preserving `yaml` syntax. So the tree-sitter parser for YAML is used for syntax.

When I'm trying to expand a snippet inside an ansible file, YAML snippets are used.

When disabling tree-sitter, the behavior is the expected one.

I'm pretty sure I have to do something with the `MiniSnippets.default_*` functions to override this behavior but I'ld prefer use the default behavior (using `snippets/*.json` files).

### Reproduction

1. Create separate 'nvim-repro' config directory:
    - '~/.config/nvim-repro/' on Unix
    - '~/AppData/Local/nvim-repro/' on Windows

2. Inside 'nvim-repro' directory create a file named 'init.lua'.
   Populate it with the following content:

    ```lua
    -- Clone latest 'mini.nvim' (requires Git CLI installed)
    vim.cmd('echo "Installing `mini.nvim`" | redraw')
    local mini_path = vim.fn.stdpath("data") .. "/site/pack/deps/start/mini.nvim"
    local clone_cmd = { "git", "clone", "--depth=1", "https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim", mini_path }
    vim.fn.system(clone_cmd)
    vim.cmd('echo "`mini.nvim` is installed" | redraw')

    -- Make sure 'mini.nvim' is available
    vim.cmd("packadd mini.nvim")
    require("mini.deps").setup()

    -- Add extra setup steps needed to reproduce the behavior
    -- Use `MiniDeps.add('user/repo')` to install another plugin from GitHub
    MiniDeps.add("mfussenegger/nvim-ansible")
    MiniDeps.add({
    	source = "nvim-treesitter/nvim-treesitter",
    	hooks = {
    		post_checkout = function()
    			vim.cmd("TSUpdate")
    		end,
    	},
    })

    require("mini.snippets").setup({
    	snippets = {
    		require("mini.snippets").gen_loader.from_file(vim.fn.stdpath("config") .. "/snippets/global.json"),
    		require("mini.snippets").gen_loader.from_lang({ lang_patterns = { ["yaml.ansible"] = { "ansible.json" } } }),
    	},
    })

    require("nvim-treesitter.configs").setup({
    	ensure_installed = { "yaml" },
    	highlight = { enable = true },
    })
    ```

3. Create a `snippets` directory inside `nvim-repro` and create the two following
   files: `ansible.json` and `yaml.json`
   Populate `ansible.json` as follow:
   ```json
   {
     "test": {
       "prefix": "test",
       "body": "this is an ansible snippet",
       "description": "'test' snippet for ansible"
     }
   }
   ```
   Populate `yaml.json` as follow:
   ```json
   {
     "test": {
       "prefix": "test",
       "body": "this is a yaml snippet",
       "description": "'test' snippet for yaml"
     }
   }
   ```

4. Run `NVIM_APPNAME=nvim-repro nvim` (i.e. execute `nvim` with `NVIM_APPNAME` environment variable set to "nvim-repro").
   Wait for all dependencies to install.

5. Open an ansible file (or `test.yml` and force `filetype` to `yaml.ansible`).
   Try to expand the `test` snippet.

comment_data.body:
Thanks for the issue!

This is already possible and indeed requires to use `default_prepare()`. Here is one approach:

```lua
local my_prepare = function(raw_snippets)
  local _, cont = MiniSnippets.default_prepare({})
  cont.lang = vim.bo.filetype == "yaml.ansible" and "yaml.ansible" or cont.lang
  return MiniSnippets.default_prepare(raw_snippets, { context = cont })
end

require("mini.snippets").setup({
  snippets = {
    require("mini.snippets").gen_loader.from_file(vim.fn.stdpath("config") .. "/snippets/global.json"),
    require("mini.snippets").gen_loader.from_lang({ lang_patterns = { ["yaml.ansible"] = { "ansible.json" } } }),
  },
  expand = { prepare = my_prepare },
})
```

This is a documented way of [adjusting context used for snippet preparation](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/b21cd5b1b330844e4c4b93d65e99ecb7c79a63c9/doc/mini-snippets.txt#L686-L691) and I think is a fairly reasonable way to provide flexible customization here.

Providing an option to disable usage of tree-sitter language as `lang` in context doesn't look like a good idea. Mostly because it will make impossible to have "local snippet context" inside injected languages (like in markdown code blocks). As there are reasonably concise workarounds for handful (at the moment) cases, I think the current design is okay.

Closing as already possible.

title: Add parameter to override treesitter parser in favor of filetype
